messages.subject: Random effect component
parts:
Good evening everyone,

I am trying to implement in INLA a model that was defined in Nimble (Stoner et al. 2019). The model is as follows:

### Nimble code
sim_code_2 = nimbleCode({ 
 for(i in 1:N){ 
 lambda[i] <- exp(a0 + a1 * x[i] + phi[i]) 
 pi[i] <- ilogit(b0 + b1 * v[i] + gamma[i]) 
 z[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i] * pi[i]) 
gamma[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = epsilon) } 
 phi[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj = adj[1:l_adj], num = n_adj[1:N], tau = tau, zero_mean = 1) 
 a0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10) 
 a1 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10) 
 b0 ~ dnorm(prior_mean, sd = prior_sd) 
 b1 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10) 
 nu ~ T(dnorm(0, 1), 0, 1) 
 tau <- 1 / nu^2 epsilon ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 1), 0,) })

My INLA code is as follows:

# Defined function 
func <- function(beta0, v1, beta1, theta) { 
 aa <- beta0 + v1 * beta1 + theta 
 return(-log(1 + exp(-aa))) } 

 # Model definition 

 cmp <- ~ intercept(1, model = "linear", mean.linear = 0, prec.linear = 0.1) + 
 alpha1(main = x1, model = "linear", mean.linear = 0, prec.linear = 0.1) + 
 b0(main = 1, model = "linear", mean.linear = b0_mean, prec.linear = 1 / (b0_sd)^2) +
 b1(main = 1, model = "linear", mean.linear = 0, prec.linear = 0.1) + 
 spatial(loc, model = "besag", graph = sim_graph, constr = T, #hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(1, 0.1))), scale.model = T, adjust.for.con.comp = TRUE) + 
theta(loc, model = "iid", constr = F, hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(1, 0.001)))) 

 # Formula 
 formula_poiss_media <- z ~ intercept + alpha1 + spatial + func(b0, v1, b1, theta)

However, I am getting very different results for the coverage of b1. 

I probably made a mistake in defining the causal effect.

Does anyone have any ideas and can help me?

Thanks

Greta

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effect component
parts:
Hi,
not sure if this is the only difference between your Nimble model and
your INLA model, but you have prec.linear=0.1 in the INLA code but
sd=10 in the Nimble code, which corresponds to precision=0.01, not
0.1.
There might be more differences; I would expect the "besag"
parameterisation & priors to be difficult to be identical between the
two specifications, for example; it's unclear whether you've commented
out parts of your "spatial" model hyperparameter settings, and
scale.model also changes the interpretation of the parameters (but in
the INLA context, you likely are better off using it anyway).
Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effect component
parts:
Another possible difference:
"besag" in INLA is an ICAR(1) model, and you're also imposing a
sum-to-zero constraint (which is sensible for ICAR), but the name
"car" in your Nimble model leads me to believe that your Nimble model
uses a proper CAR(1) model, which is not the same thing. If that's the
case, perhaps switch to "besagproper" or "besagproper2" (but again,
getting the same priors will likely be a challenge, especially if
neither of those two INLA models are parameterised the same as the
Nimble version).
Finn
